summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a known 2.6 cm hepatocellular carcinoma was admitted for transarterial chemoembolization (TACE). The procedure was performed successfully via right femoral access with doxorubicin-loaded beads, and she recovered without complications. Post-procedure, she experienced expected abdominal cramping and transient symptoms of alcohol withdrawal, including headache and auditory hallucinations, which resolved with supportive care and detoxification protocol. Her mental status improved, and liver function remained stable despite a transient rise in AST. She was managed with pain control, continued cirrhosis medications, and psychiatric support. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for MRI and ongoing liver and mental health care.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, continuous
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
